name: Hydrogen
description: The lightest element and the most abundant in the universe. Its single proton and electron make it the starting point for atomic models; water (H₂O) and most organic molecules contain it. Hydrogen (H) is a reactive non-metal in period 1, group 1. It is a gas at room temperature.
dataNote: Gas density is given in g/L at 0 °C and 101.325 kPa.

name: Helium
description: A noble gas with a completely filled first electron shell, so it is chemically inert. It is formed in stars by nuclear fusion and on Earth by radioactive alpha decay. Helium (He) is a noble gas in period 1, group 18. It is a gas at room temperature.
dataNote: Gas density is given in g/L at 0 °C and 101.325 kPa.

name: Lithium
description: The lightest metal. Like all alkali metals it readily loses one electron; lithium compounds are central to rechargeable batteries. Lithium (Li) is an alkali metal in period 2, group 1. It is a solid at room temperature.

name: Beryllium
description: A light, stiff alkaline-earth metal found in the mineral beryl (emerald is a gem variety of beryl). Beryllium (Be) is an alkaline-earth metal in period 2, group 2. It is a solid at room temperature.

name: Boron
description: A metalloid that forms strong covalent networks; borosilicate laboratory glass contains boron oxide. Boron (B) is a metalloid in period 2, group 13. It is a solid at room temperature.

name: Carbon
description: Forms more compounds than any other element because carbon atoms bond strongly to each other. Graphite and diamond are two allotropes with very different properties: graphite conducts electricity, diamond is an electrical insulator. Carbon (C) is a reactive non-metal in period 2, group 14. It is a solid at room temperature.
dataNote: Density and melting data refer to graphite; carbon sublimes at atmospheric pressure (about 3900 K).

name: Nitrogen
description: Makes up about 78 % of the air by volume as N₂ molecules held together by a very strong triple bond. Nitrogen (N) is a reactive non-metal in period 2, group 15. It is a gas at room temperature.
dataNote: Gas density is given in g/L at 0 °C and 101.325 kPa.

name: Oxygen
description: About 21 % of air by volume and the most abundant element in Earth's crust by mass, mostly bound in silicate and oxide minerals. Oxygen (O) is a reactive non-metal in period 2, group 16. It is a gas at room temperature.
dataNote: Gas density is given in g/L at 0 °C and 101.325 kPa.

name: Fluorine
description: The most electronegative element; it reacts with almost every other element. Fluorine (F) is a reactive non-metal in period 2, group 17. It is a gas at room temperature.
dataNote: Gas density is given in g/L at 0 °C and 101.325 kPa.

name: Neon
description: A noble gas; electric discharges through neon produce its characteristic red-orange glow. Neon (Ne) is a noble gas in period 2, group 18. It is a gas at room temperature.
dataNote: Gas density is given in g/L at 0 °C and 101.325 kPa.

name: Sodium
description: A soft, very reactive alkali metal. It never occurs free in nature; sodium chloride (table salt) is its best-known compound. Sodium (Na) is an alkali metal in period 3, group 1. It is a solid at room temperature.

name: Magnesium
description: A light alkaline-earth metal; the magnesium ion is at the centre of the chlorophyll molecule. Magnesium (Mg) is an alkaline-earth metal in period 3, group 2. It is a solid at room temperature.

name: Aluminium
description: The most abundant metal in Earth's crust. A thin oxide layer protects it from further corrosion. Aluminium (Al) is a post-transition metal in period 3, group 13. It is a solid at room temperature.

name: Silicon
description: A metalloid and semiconductor, the second most abundant element in the crust. Sand and quartz are mostly silicon dioxide (SiO₂). Silicon (Si) is a metalloid in period 3, group 14. It is a solid at room temperature.

name: Phosphorus
description: Essential for life (DNA, ATP, bone mineral). Elemental phosphorus exists as several allotropes with very different reactivity. Phosphorus (P) is a reactive non-metal in period 3, group 15. It is a solid at room temperature.

name: Sulfur
description: A yellow non-metal found near volcanoes and in sulfide ores such as chalcopyrite (CuFeS₂). Sulfur (S) is a reactive non-metal in period 3, group 16. It is a solid at room temperature.

name: Chlorine
description: A reactive halogen. Chlorine gas is toxic, but chloride ions are harmless in table salt and essential to living things. Chlorine (Cl) is a reactive non-metal in period 3, group 17. It is a gas at room temperature.
dataNote: Gas density is given in g/L at 0 °C and 101.325 kPa.

name: Argon
description: The most abundant noble gas in air (about 0.93 %), produced by radioactive decay of potassium-40. Argon (Ar) is a noble gas in period 3, group 18. It is a gas at room temperature.
dataNote: Gas density is given in g/L at 0 °C and 101.325 kPa.

name: Potassium
description: An alkali metal essential to nerve signalling. Potassium salts give a lilac flame. Potassium (K) is an alkali metal in period 4, group 1. It is a solid at room temperature.

name: Calcium
description: An alkaline-earth metal. Limestone, calcite, chalk and dripstone are calcium carbonate; bones contain calcium phosphate minerals. Calcium (Ca) is an alkaline-earth metal in period 4, group 2. It is a solid at room temperature.

name: Scandium
description: Scandium (Sc) is a transition metal in period 4, group 3. It is a solid at room temperature.

name: Titanium
description: A strong, low-density transition metal resistant to corrosion. Titanium (Ti) is a transition metal in period 4, group 4. It is a solid at room temperature.

name: Vanadium
description: Vanadium (V) is a transition metal in period 4, group 5. It is a solid at room temperature.

name: Chromium
description: A hard transition metal used in stainless steel and chrome plating. Chromium (Cr) is a transition metal in period 4, group 6. It is a solid at room temperature.

name: Manganese
description: A transition metal important in steel-making and found in many oxidation states. Manganese (Mn) is a transition metal in period 4, group 7. It is a solid at room temperature.

name: Iron
description: The most common element on Earth by mass (much of the core is iron). Iron is smelted from oxide ores such as hematite (Fe₂O₃) and magnetite (Fe₃O₄) and is ferromagnetic. Iron (Fe) is a transition metal in period 4, group 8. It is a solid at room temperature.

name: Cobalt
description: A ferromagnetic transition metal used in magnets and as the blue colouring of glass and ceramics. Cobalt (Co) is a transition metal in period 4, group 9. It is a solid at room temperature.

name: Nickel
description: A ferromagnetic, corrosion-resistant metal used in stainless steel and coins. Nickel (Ni) is a transition metal in period 4, group 10. It is a solid at room temperature.

name: Copper
description: A reddish metal with the second-highest electrical conductivity of any element (after silver), which is why electrical wiring is made of copper. Copper (Cu) is a transition metal in period 4, group 11. It is a solid at room temperature.

name: Zinc
description: Used to galvanise steel against corrosion and in brass (a copper–zinc alloy). Zinc (Zn) is a transition metal in period 4, group 12. It is a solid at room temperature.

name: Gallium
description: A metal that melts at about 30 °C, just above room temperature. Gallium (Ga) is a post-transition metal in period 4, group 13. It is a solid at room temperature.

name: Germanium
description: A semiconductor metalloid used in early transistors and in infrared optics. Germanium (Ge) is a metalloid in period 4, group 14. It is a solid at room temperature.

name: Arsenic
description: A metalloid; many arsenic compounds are highly toxic. Arsenic (As) is a metalloid in period 4, group 15. It is a solid at room temperature.
dataNote: Arsenic sublimes at atmospheric pressure (about 887 K).

name: Selenium
description: Selenium (Se) is a reactive non-metal in period 4, group 16. It is a solid at room temperature.

name: Bromine
description: One of only two elements that are liquid at room temperature (with mercury). Bromine (Br) is a reactive non-metal in period 4, group 17. It is a liquid at room temperature.

name: Krypton
description: A noble gas used in some lighting. Krypton (Kr) is a noble gas in period 4, group 18. It is a gas at room temperature.
dataNote: Gas density is given in g/L at 0 °C and 101.325 kPa.

name: Rubidium
description: Rubidium (Rb) is an alkali metal in period 5, group 1. It is a solid at room temperature.

name: Strontium
description: Strontium salts give fireworks a bright red colour. Strontium (Sr) is an alkaline-earth metal in period 5, group 2. It is a solid at room temperature.

name: Yttrium
description: Yttrium (Y) is a transition metal in period 5, group 3. It is a solid at room temperature.

name: Zirconium
description: Zirconium (Zr) is a transition metal in period 5, group 4. It is a solid at room temperature.

name: Niobium
description: Niobium (Nb) is a transition metal in period 5, group 5. It is a solid at room temperature.

name: Molybdenum
description: Molybdenum (Mo) is a transition metal in period 5, group 6. It is a solid at room temperature.

name: Technetium
description: The lightest element with no stable isotopes; most technetium is produced artificially. Technetium (Tc) is a transition metal in period 5, group 7. It is a solid at room temperature. It is radioactive; only trace amounts occur in nature.
dataNote: No standard atomic weight: the value shown is the mass number of the longest-lived known isotope.

name: Ruthenium
description: Ruthenium (Ru) is a transition metal in period 5, group 8. It is a solid at room temperature.

name: Rhodium
description: Rhodium (Rh) is a transition metal in period 5, group 9. It is a solid at room temperature.

name: Palladium
description: Palladium (Pd) is a transition metal in period 5, group 10. It is a solid at room temperature.

name: Silver
description: The best electrical and thermal conductor of all metals. Silver (Ag) is a transition metal in period 5, group 11. It is a solid at room temperature.

name: Cadmium
description: Cadmium (Cd) is a transition metal in period 5, group 12. It is a solid at room temperature.

name: Indium
description: Indium (In) is a post-transition metal in period 5, group 13. It is a solid at room temperature.

name: Tin
description: A soft metal used in solder and to coat (tin-plate) steel; bronze is a copper–tin alloy. Tin (Sn) is a post-transition metal in period 5, group 14. It is a solid at room temperature.

name: Antimony
description: Antimony (Sb) is a metalloid in period 5, group 15. It is a solid at room temperature.

name: Tellurium
description: Tellurium (Te) is a metalloid in period 5, group 16. It is a solid at room temperature.

name: Iodine
description: A halogen that forms violet vapour when heated; iodide is needed for thyroid hormones. Iodine (I) is a reactive non-metal in period 5, group 17. It is a solid at room temperature.

name: Xenon
description: A noble gas that, unusually, forms some stable compounds with fluorine and oxygen. Xenon (Xe) is a noble gas in period 5, group 18. It is a gas at room temperature.
dataNote: Gas density is given in g/L at 0 °C and 101.325 kPa.

name: Cesium
description: A very reactive alkali metal; the SI second is defined using a transition of caesium-133 atoms. Cesium (Cs) is an alkali metal in period 6, group 1. It is a solid at room temperature.

name: Barium
description: Barium compounds give a green flame; barium sulfate is used in medical X-ray imaging. Barium (Ba) is an alkaline-earth metal in period 6, group 2. It is a solid at room temperature.

name: Tantalum

name: Tungsten
description: Tungsten has the highest melting point of all metals, which is why it was used for light-bulb filaments. Tungsten (W) is a transition metal in period 6, group 6. It is a solid at room temperature.

name: Rhenium
description: Rhenium (Re) is a transition metal in period 6, group 7. It is a solid at room temperature.

name: Osmium
description: Osmium (Os) is a transition metal in period 6, group 8. It is a solid at room temperature.

name: Iridium

name: Platinum
description: A dense, unreactive precious metal and important catalyst. Platinum (Pt) is a transition metal in period 6, group 10. It is a solid at room temperature.

name: Gold
description: A dense, very unreactive precious metal that is found as native (uncombined) metal. It is an excellent conductor and does not tarnish. Gold (Au) is a transition metal in period 6, group 11. It is a solid at room temperature.

name: Mercury
description: The only metal that is liquid at room temperature. Mercury and its compounds are toxic. Mercury (Hg) is a transition metal in period 6, group 12. It is a liquid at room temperature.

name: Thallium
description: Thallium (Tl) is a post-transition metal in period 6, group 13. It is a solid at room temperature.

name: Lead
description: A dense, soft metal. Lead is toxic, so its former uses in paint and petrol have been phased out. Lead (Pb) is a post-transition metal in period 6, group 14. It is a solid at room temperature.

name: Bismuth
description: The heaviest element with a practically stable isotope (bismuth-209 decays with an extremely long half-life). Bismuth (Bi) is a post-transition metal in period 6, group 15. It is a solid at room temperature.

name: Polonium
description: Polonium (Po) is a post-transition metal in period 6, group 16. It is a solid at room temperature. It is radioactive and occurs naturally only as a short-lived product of uranium and thorium decay.
dataNote: No standard atomic weight: the value shown is the mass number of the longest-lived known isotope.

name: Astatine
description: Astatine (At) is a metalloid in period 6, group 17. It is a solid at room temperature. It is radioactive and occurs naturally only as a short-lived product of uranium and thorium decay.
dataNote: Bulk astatine has never been observed; density and melting point are estimates. No standard atomic weight: the value shown is the mass number of the longest-lived known isotope.

name: Radon
description: A radioactive noble gas formed by the decay of radium; it can accumulate in poorly ventilated buildings. Radon (Rn) is a noble gas in period 6, group 18. It is a gas at room temperature. It is radioactive and occurs naturally only as a short-lived product of uranium and thorium decay.
dataNote: No standard atomic weight: the value shown is the mass number of the longest-lived known isotope. Gas density is given in g/L at 0 °C and 101.325 kPa.

name: Francium
description: Francium (Fr) is an alkali metal in period 7, group 1. It is a solid at room temperature. It is radioactive and occurs naturally only as a short-lived product of uranium and thorium decay.
dataNote: Bulk francium has never been observed; its melting point and density are estimates. No standard atomic weight: the value shown is the mass number of the longest-lived known isotope.

name: Radium

dataNote: No standard atomic weight: the value shown is the mass number of the longest-lived known isotope.
